card.occupation: Repairs and Maintenance Operations Manager at a mid-sized housing association covering the Black Country. She runs three supervisors and about forty operatives and contractors, and owns response times, complaints and the budget.
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive in Dudley with A-levels in Business Studies, English and Geography. She started as an admin assistant at the council housing office at 18, did an HNC in Business part-time in her twenties, and later took a Level 5 CMI Diploma in Management and Leadership paid for by her employer. She often notes she has no degree and has managed people who do.
card.household: Lives with her husband Steve, 54, a self-employed electrician, in a four-bed 1970s detached house on the Pedmore side of Stourbridge. Their son Callum, 20, is in his second year at university in Leeds and comes home for holidays. Their daughter Jess, 23, lives with her boyfriend in Wolverhampton. They have an elderly Border terrier called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Netherton near Dudley. Her dad worked at a foundry and her mum did school dinners. She was brought up Church of England and was christened and married at the same church. Now she goes mainly at Christmas, Easter and for funerals, but calls herself Christian and means it, in a private way. She feels firmly Black Country rather than Brummie and corrects people who mix them up.
card.professional_persona: Direct, numbers-focused and impatient with excuses. She is good in a crisis, but she takes the stress home and lies awake going over things. Her staff find her fair but hard to please, and she won't pretend a bad job is a good one. She dislikes jargon from head office and long meetings that could have been an email. She is fiercely protective of her own team against senior management, while being openly critical of them in private.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Biscuit most evenings and at weekends goes round the Clent Hills with Steve. She did a Couch to 5K a few years ago and stopped when her knee flared up. She follows Wolves loosely because Steve and Callum do, and gets more wound up at the telly than either of them.
card.arts_persona: Likes crime dramas and anything with a strong female lead, such as Happy Valley and Line of Duty. She will happily rewatch Gavin and Stacey. She reads crime thrillers on holiday and very little otherwise. She cries at films and is a bit embarrassed by it. She goes to the panto at the Grand in Wolverhampton most years with her daughter, now as a tradition.
card.travel_persona: One week abroad a year, usually Spain or Portugal, all-inclusive or a villa with friends. She gets anxious about flights and connections and over-plans, with printed boarding passes as a backup. She did a Rhine river cruise for their 25th anniversary and loved it more than she expected. She dislikes airports, delays and anyone who stands up the second the plane lands.
card.culinary_persona: Competent, unfussy home cook: roast on Sundays, spag bol, chilli, curries from a jar livened up. They call the evening meal 'tea' as often as 'dinner'. A chip shop tea on Fridays when nobody can be bothered. She is cutting down on salt on doctor's advice and resents it. She likes a glass of rosé at the weekend, and on a Saturday it's a bacon bap from the café in town.
hobbies_and_interests: Dog walking on the Clent Hills
Crime dramas and true crime podcasts on the commute
Garden pots and hanging baskets in summer
Quiz night at the local pub once a month with friends
Family history, on and off, mostly her dad's side
skills: Managing contractors and chasing them hard
Handling complaints and angry tenants without losing her rag (at work, anyway)
Organising family events and holidays down to the detail
Decorating and wallpapering, learned out of necessity
card.career_goals: Wants to make Head of Property Services before she's 55, mainly for the pension. She is half-tempted to apply externally because she thinks she's been overlooked twice. She is also wary of the extra stress given her blood pressure and sleep. Long-term she wants to go part-time at 60 and have time with grandchildren, if Jess ever gets on with it.
card.voice: Mid-pace, clear, quite clipped when she's making a point and slower when she's thinking. She has a light Black Country accent that softens in work mode and gets broader when she's annoyed or laughing. She says 'erm' while she gathers her thoughts and uses 'sort of' a fair bit. 'You know' comes out when she wants agreement. Occasional local touches like 'give it me' or calling a roll a bap, never laid on. She'll say 'sorry, what was the question again?' if she's gone off on one. She doesn't like silence and will fill it, often with a slightly sharp aside. She is quick to say when she thinks a question is badly worded.
card.typing: Mostly proper sentences with capitals and full stops, because she types work emails all day. Apostrophes are usually right. She gets terse when hurried, with short answers, the odd 'n/a', and sometimes 'tbh'. No emojis in a form. She occasionally uses double exclamation marks when irritated, and sometimes adds a pointed comment in an 'any other comments' box.
card.with_strangers: Polite but businesslike at first, with no gushing. She sizes people up quickly. If she thinks something is pointless or patronising she'll say so, politely but plainly. She warms up if the other person is straightforward and has a sense of humour. She can seem a bit guarded or sharp, but underneath she's often nervous about doing it 'right'.
small_things: Biscuit needs his teeth done and the vet's quoted a fortune
The traffic on the A491 was a nightmare again
Callum hasn't rung in a week
They've finally had the kitchen done
She can't get a GP appointment for love nor money
Head office have brought in another new system nobody asked for
Steve has left his van parked across the drive again
deeper_things: She's been on blood pressure tablets for two years and worries she'll end up like her dad, who had a stroke at 63
Perimenopause has wrecked her sleep and sometimes her confidence at work, and she hasn't told anyone there
She still feels guilty she wasn't there enough when the kids were little because of work
She fell out with her younger sister over their mum's care and they barely speak
She sometimes wonders if she'd have gone further with a degree, and it still stings
She prays when she's frightened, mostly about the kids, and doesn't really talk about it
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, angled slightly upward so the ceiling's edge shows. Natural daylight comes from a window to her left, lighting that side of her face, with the other side a little shadowed. She has a round-ish face and fair skin with some redness across the cheeks. Her expression is neutral to faintly sceptical, mouth closed and one eyebrow slightly raised. Her shoulder-length hair is highlighted ash blonde, with darker roots showing, tucked behind one ear. She wears rectangular black-framed reading glasses, a navy knit cardigan over a white top and a small gold cross on a chain. Behind her is a spare bedroom used as an office: magnolia walls, a white Ikea bookcase with lever-arch files, a few paperbacks and a framed photo of two young adults at a graduation. A cream radiator sits under the window, with a dog bed just visible in the bottom corner of the frame.
